title: A targeted mass spectrometry method for the accurate label-free quantification of immunogenic gluten peptides produced during simulated digestion of food matrices
author: Ogilvie, Larsen, et al.
materials: Each peptide was analysed individually in full scan data-dependent analysis (DDA) tandem fragmentation (MS/MS) mode using the ionisation and fragmentation parameters described in Table 5. Each peptide's retention time, dominant charge state and mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) were defined by examining the raw spectra. In silico MS/MS was undertaken using the PROTEOMICS TOOLKIT fragment ion calculator (or equivalent software). Direct sequence fragment ions (b+ and y+) were identified from the raw spectra by matching the in silico MS/MS ions to those experimentally observed. The highest intensity 4–5 direct sequence fragment ions were selected as identifier and quantifier ions for use in data processing. This optimised PRM and sample preparation method can accurately quantify peptides P1-P6 with an LOD between 0.027–0.161 µg mL−1 (peptide dependent) and LOQ between 0.218–0.769 (Table 6). As highlighted in Fig. 3, P1-P6 display a linear relationship between peptide concentration and peptide abundance between 0.5 µg mL−1 and 10 µg mL−1, which extends to the defined LOQ. As recommended by the ICH1, Table 7 displays the typical regression properties of the calibration curves used to extrapolate the peptide abundance to concentration. The PRM method has minimal day-to-day variability, which is highlighted in Table 8 by a CV of <10%. Additionally, P1-P6 do not show matrix effects due to the efficiency of the SPE sample preparation method described above. This accurate MS method builds on the relative MS method developed by van den Broeck 2005 [6]. steps.title: Prepare stock digestive fluids
steps.instruction: Formulate oral, gastric and intestinal fluid stock solutions at 1.25 × the working concentrations using the following component concentrations (mmol L⁻¹): Oral: KCl 15.0, KH₂PO₄ 3.7, NaHCO₃ 13.6, NaCl –47.2, MgCl₂·(H₂O) 0.6, (NH₄)₂CO₃ 0.0, pH 7.0 (3 % B). Gastric: KCl 16.9, KH₂PO₄ 0.9, NaHCO₃ 25.0, NaCl 38.4, MgCl₂·(H₂O) 0.15, (NH₄)₂CO₃ 0.06, pH 3.0 (0 % B). Intestinal: KCl 6.8, KH₂PO₄ 0.8, NaHCO₃ 5.0, NaCl 33.0, MgCl₂·(H₂O) 0.33, (NH₄)₂CO₃ 0.5, pH 7.0 (3 % B). Store stocks at –20 °C for up to one year. Prepare each fluid 25 min before use and pre‑warm to 37 °C (intestinal fluid is prepared after 95 min of gastric digestion).

steps.title: Freeze‑dry and rehydrate bread
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry the bread sample. Rehydrate the freeze‑dried bread at a 1.25 : 4 (w/v) ratio with Milli‑Q water (e.g., 1.25 g bread + 4 mL water). If feasible, add an isotopically‑labelled internal standard at this stage.

steps.title: Add oral fluid and chew
steps.instruction: Add oral fluid at a 1 : 1 (v/w) ratio to the original bread weight (e.g., 1.25 mL oral fluid to 1.25 g bread). Triturate with a fork for 2 min to simulate chewing.

steps.title: Add gastric fluid and incubate
steps.instruction: Add gastric fluid at a 1 : 1 (v/w) ratio to the total solution (e.g., 2.5 mL gastric fluid to 1.25 g bread). Incubate for 2 h at 37 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Add intestinal fluid and incubate
steps.instruction: Add intestinal fluid at a 1 : 1 (v/w) ratio to the total solution (e.g., 5 mL intestinal fluid to 1.25 g bread). Adjust for any volume loss during the gastric phase. Incubate for 2 h at 37 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Quench digestion aliquots
steps.instruction: At each desired time point, remove an aliquot of digesta and quench by adding TFA from a 12 % (v/v) stock to achieve a final concentration of 0.1 % (v/v). Vortex 5 s, snap‑freeze in liquid N₂, and store at –20 °C (up to 1 yr). Add the calculated volume of TFA to all sampling tubes at the start of the experiment to ensure consistent quenching.

steps.title: Thaw, vortex and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Defrost digesta on ice, vortex briefly, then centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 10 min.

steps.title: Spike internal standard
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of supernatant to a new tube and add P1H from a 50 µg mL⁻¹ stock to reach a final concentration of 3 µg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Solid‑phase extraction (SPE)
steps.instruction: Purify the spiked supernatant using Strata‑XL 100 µm RP SPE tubes (30 mg mL⁻¹, Phenomenex) following Table 4. Dry the SPE cartridge at least 30 s between each step.

steps.title: Filter eluate and store
steps.instruction: Collect the eluate (Step 5) and filter through a SINGLE StEP™ filter vial (Thomson Instrument Company™). Store filtered samples at 4 °C for 2–3 days or at –20 °C for longer periods.

steps.title: Set up PRM LC‑MS method
steps.instruction: In Thermo Xcalibur, create a PRM method using the transitions listed in Table 10, the chromatography schedule in Table 9, and instrument parameters from Table 5 (spray voltage 35 kV, spray current 17 µA, aux gas 10, sheath gas 45, scan range 108–4015 m/z, resolving power 70 000, capillary temp 320 °C, NCE stepped 18–27 %).

steps.title: Prepare external standard curve
steps.instruction: Pool synthetic peptides P1–P6 to a 50 µg mL⁻¹ stock, then serially dilute with SPE eluate to 10, 5, 2, 1, 0.5 µg mL⁻¹ (final curve 0.5–10 µg mL⁻¹).

steps.title: Condition LC column
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat the LC column to 40 °C and equilibrate with mobile phase A (99.9 % H₂O, 0.1 % FA) at 97 % and mobile phase B (99.9 % ACN, 0.1 % FA) at 3 % flow 0.3 mL min⁻¹.

steps.title: Inject standards, blank and samples
steps.instruction: Inject 2 µL of each standard (run three replicates) and a 2 µL blank to check carry‑over. Then inject 2 µL of each SPE‑prepared digested sample. Run the external standard curve every 10–15 samples.

steps.title: Process PRM data
steps.instruction: Process raw PRM files in Xcalibur Quan Browser using an automatic processing method (.pmd) that contains the transitions from Table 10. Visually validate peak integration and the standard curve, then export peptide concentrations. Apply correction for the SPE dilution factor and P1H suppression to obtain final concentrations.
